scenes.anchor_text:
“Above silence, the illuminating storms—dying storms— illuminate the silence above.”
The above sample is noteworthy as it is a ketek, a complex form of holy Vorin poem.
scenes.scene_description: A visualization of the ketek, depicting a dying storm illuminating the silence above. The focus is on the atmospheric phenomenon rather than any specific characters.

scenes.anchor_text: The fact that this one was uttered by an illiterate, dying Herdazian in a language he barely spoke should be of particular note. There is no record of this particular ketek in any repository of Vorin poetry,
scenes.scene_description: A dimly lit Ardents' library, highlighting the vast collection of Vorin poetry where the ketek is absent. The scene emphasizes the rarity and unexpected origin of the poem.

scenes.anchor_text: We leave it to His Majesty’s mind, on a strong day, to puzzle out the meaning of why the storms might be important, and what the poem may mean by indicating that there is silence both above and below said storms.
scenes.scene_description: A majestic, cloud-piercing palace atop a mountain peak. Storms rage below and distant stars are visible above, symbolizing the 'silence both above and below said storms'.
